command: import importlib.metadata as m,json,sys; from pathlib import Path; d=m.distribution("evalscope"); metadata=[p for p in d.files if p.name=="METADATA" and str(p.parent).endswith(".dist-info")]; assert len(metadata)==1; print(json.dumps({"version":d.version,"name":d.metadata["Name"],"package_location":str(Path(d.locate_file("evalscope")).resolve()),"metadata_directory":str(Path(d.locate_file(metadata[0])).resolve().parent),"executable":sys.executable,"prefix":sys.prefix,"base_prefix":sys.base_prefix,"python_version":sys.version,"cache_tag":sys.implementation.cache_tag}))

limitations: This checks dependency availability and byte identities, not inference, client operation, throughput or model quality.
The single Python subprocess reads distribution metadata only; evalscope and its perf/CLI modules are not imported or executed.
The old HTTP version is matched; perf/CLI source hashes are new prospective bindings, not proof of historical package bytes.
No model file is hashed or opened for content. Selected model and tokenizer files are checked only for readability and metadata.
Only the selected distribution sources/metadata and interpreter are bound; transitive packages, native libraries, standard library and bytecode caches are not exhaustively certified.
Absent starts/evidence refers only to this attempt, not every process or server on the machine.
